subject.title: fix(whatsapp): add chunk-idle timeout to inbound media download

question: Should WhatsApp inbound media universally fail after 30 seconds without a chunk, or should the idle budget be retuned before merge?
rationale: The implementation and proof establish that the timeout works, but code evidence cannot choose the acceptable latency-versus-delivery tradeoff for real WhatsApp media networks.

options.title: Accept the 30-second cutoff
options.body: Merge with the demonstrated Telegram-aligned idle budget and accept that exceptionally slow streams will fail instead of blocking inbound dispatch indefinitely.

options.title: Retune the cutoff
options.body: Choose a different plugin-local constant based on WhatsApp operational experience, then rerun the same timeout and progressing-stream proof.

options.title: Pause pending live calibration
options.body: Hold the PR until a live WhatsApp media stall or representative network test establishes an appropriate production budget.

recommendation.title: Accept the 30-second cutoff
recommendation.body: Merge with the demonstrated Telegram-aligned idle budget and accept that exceptionally slow streams will fail instead of blocking inbound dispatch indefinitely.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged WhatsApp inbound, session, and media-retry work makes this the strongest available owner signal for the delivery-policy choice.
